trust_decision.summary: A caller-supplied export_id is interpolated with %-formatting into a GraphQL query string literal in get_export_status, so the ID itself decides the query structure instead of being bound as a GraphQL variable.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'Export Status Lookup'. get_export_status is the only status query, and the %s sits inside export(id: "%s").

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No dismissable route exists. The only other string-built GraphQL query is _create_simple_export (src/export_manager.py:47-53), and its mutation_name is a hard-coded constant (src/export_manager.py:118,142).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Real export IDs are base64-like and contain + / = (see the in-progress ID regex). An over-tight allow-list such as [A-Za-z0-9-] would reject real IDs and break status and download calls.

O6_input_shapes: plain string export_id passed through the MCP tool argument

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make _create_simple_export take a caller-influenced field (for example a source or format option) and interpolate it into the f-string mutation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This mutation is already built with an f-string, while the asset_software sibling passes its source/format as variables (src/export_manager.py:240-247). A maintainer adding options to the simple helper could easily inline them.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Remediation export built with inline startDate/endDate instead of $input variables
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Low value: the dates are strptime-validated first (src/export_manager.py:174-186), so it adds only a how-type validation differential (strptime accepts a value whose raw string differs from the canonical date).

O9_family: GraphQL query injection (CWE-943, injection into a query language string)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_export_manager.py:139-280 (get_export_status with mocked requests.post), tests/test_mcp_server.py:83 (monkeypatched get_export_status), tests/test_graphql_client.py:35-53 (variables in body)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Switch to export(id: $id) with variables={'id': export_id}. This is also the correct fix, so there is no trap.

out_of_scope_notes: src/duckdb_loader.py:159-252 builds f-string SQL from table names and paths (marked nosec); this is a different sink and protection.
src/mcp_server.py:907-971 query_rapid7 runs arbitrary user SQL by design; this is a different sink.
